nodes.title: Import the form binding dependency
nodes.why: FormsModule supplies ngModel for the text input, while the @for and @if blocks are built into the template syntax.
nodes.alternative: Keep CommonModule solely for legacy structural directives that the template no longer uses.
nodes.tradeoff: The dependency list stays smaller, but future CommonModule pipes must be imported if they are introduced.

nodes.title: Keep todo state in a local signal
nodes.why: A signal holding the array, plus an id counter, covers add, toggle, remove, and clear-completed, and lets hasTodos and the template react to every replacement.
nodes.alternative: Keep a plain array field and rely on zone-based change detection, or introduce a service or store for one component's list.
nodes.tradeoff: A local signal is easy to test and works with OnPush; state that other components share would later move into a service that exposes the signal.

nodes.title: Reject empty todo text before updating the list
nodes.why: Trimming first prevents whitespace-only todos from entering the rendered list or persisted state.
nodes.alternative: Append every input value and clean the list later.
nodes.tradeoff: The early return adds a small branch, but it keeps downstream rendering and tests simpler.

nodes.title: Append items with stable identity
nodes.why: The generated id gives Angular @for track todo.id a stable identity for each row as items are added and removed.
nodes.alternative: Track by array index or reuse the text as an identity.
nodes.tradeoff: An id counter is small bookkeeping, but it avoids row identity drift when duplicate text or removals occur.

nodes.title: Toggle by replacing the touched todo
nodes.why: Copying only the matching todo with done flipped gives the signal a new array and the row a new object, so computed values and OnPush views see the change while other rows keep their identity.
nodes.alternative: Flip todo.done in place or bind the checkbox with [(ngModel)]="todo.done", which edits the object without changing the signal.
nodes.tradeoff: The map allocates a new array per toggle, which is negligible for a todo list and keeps every change visible to signal consumers.

nodes.title: Remove by stable id
nodes.why: Filtering by id deletes the exact row even when multiple todos have the same text.
nodes.alternative: Remove by visible label or by current array index.
nodes.tradeoff: Id-based removal needs a generated id, but it remains correct after sorting, filtering, or duplicate entries.

nodes.title: Derive the remaining active list
nodes.why: Clear completed should preserve active todos and remove only items already marked done.
nodes.alternative: Reset the entire list or manually splice completed rows in place.
nodes.tradeoff: A filter pass is simple and predictable for this list size, though very large lists might need a different data model.
